verdict.rationale: Browserbase's own `pauseWhen` lets a user define a condition under which the Agent automatically pauses a run and asks for input, and monitoring agents can alert when something breaks. These are narrow product-native condition→action behaviors, not a general rule engine. Webhooks only notify your endpoint of subscribed events, so any resulting action is user-built, and scheduled runs are a recurring schedule, not an event trigger. Neither earns credit here. Missing for 10: a general user-defined event→action rule system, documented choice of trigger events and resulting actions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: With `pauseWhen`, the Agent can pause the run, tell you what it needs, and continue exactly where it left off once you reply.
Run agents that click through your product continuously and alert you the moment something breaks.
